questions.text: Let [latex]f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} [/latex] be a function such that [latex]f(x)=\max \left\{x, x^3\right\}, x \in \mathbb{R} [/latex], where [latex]\mathbb{R} [/latex] is the set of all real numbers. The set of all points where [latex]f(x) [/latex] is NOT differentiable is
questions.solution:
Compare [latex]x[/latex] and [latex]x^3[/latex]: they are equal at [latex]x=-1,0,1[/latex]. So [latex]f(x)=x[/latex] for [latex]x\le -1[/latex], [latex]x^3[/latex] on [latex][-1,0][/latex], [latex]x[/latex] on [latex][0,1][/latex], [latex]x^3[/latex] for [latex]x\ge1[/latex].

At every switching point the two pieces have different slopes ([latex]\frac{d}{dx}x=1[/latex], [latex]\frac{d}{dx}x^3=3x^2[/latex]):
- [latex]x=-1[/latex]: slopes [latex]1[/latex] and [latex]3[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner
- [latex]x=0[/latex]: slopes [latex]0[/latex] and [latex]1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner
- [latex]x=1[/latex]: slopes [latex]1[/latex] and [latex]3[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner

Everywhere else [latex]f[/latex] is a polynomial, hence differentiable.

Answer: [latex]\{-1,0,1\}[/latex]

questions.text:
The product of all eigenvalues of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 2 & 3\\ 
4 & 5 &6 \\ 
7 &8  & 9
\end{bmatrix}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Product of all eigenvalues [latex]=\det(A)[/latex].

[latex]\det(A)=1(45-48)-2(36-42)+3(32-35)=-3+12-9=0[/latex]

(Quick check: [latex]R_1+R_3=2R_2[/latex], so the rows are dependent and the matrix is singular.)

Answer: 0

questions.text: Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2's complement format. In this system, two integers [latex]A [/latex] and [latex]B [/latex] are represented as [latex]A=01010 [/latex] and [latex]B=11010 [/latex]. Which one of the following operations will result in either an arithmetic overflow or an arithmetic underflow?
questions.solution:
With 5-bit 2's complement the range is [latex]-16[/latex] to [latex]+15[/latex].

[latex]A=01010=+10[/latex], [latex]B=11010=-6[/latex].

- [latex]A+B=4[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- [latex]A-B=10+6=16[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] exceeds +15, overflow
- [latex]B-A=-16[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits (lowest value)
- [latex]2B=-12[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits

Answer: A [latex]-[/latex] B

questions.text: Consider a permutation sampled uniformly at random from the set of all permutations of [latex]\{1,2,3, \cdots, n\} [/latex] for some [latex]n \geq 4 [/latex]. Let [latex]X [/latex] be the event that 1 occurs before 2 in the permutation, and [latex]Y [/latex] the event that 3 occurs before 4 . Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
By symmetry, 1 is before 2 in half of all permutations, so [latex]P(X)=\frac12[/latex]; similarly [latex]P(Y)=\frac12[/latex].

The relative order of {1,2} and the relative order of {3,4} involve different elements, and all 4 combinations (12/21 with 34/43) are equally likely, so [latex]P(X\cap Y)=\frac14=P(X)P(Y)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] independent.

- Not mutually exclusive: 1 2 3 4 [latex]\ldots[/latex] satisfies both.
- Neither must occur: 2 1 4 3 [latex]\ldots[/latex] satisfies none.
- Equally likely, so X is not more likely than Y.

Answer: X and Y are independent

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Cycle stealing: DMA takes one bus cycle and moves one word [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Burst mode keeps the bus for the whole block (no repeated bus requests), so it has higher throughput for bulk transfer [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Programmed I/O has better CPU utilization than interrupt-driven I/O [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE. In programmed I/O the CPU keeps polling the device status and wastes cycles; interrupt-driven I/O lets the CPU do other work until the device interrupts.
- Vectored interrupts give the ISR address directly (no polling to find the device), so ISR starts faster [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Programmed I/O has better CPU utilization than interrupt driven I/O (FALSE)
